syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Belgium and Sri Lanka: two diverse societies

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the linguistic composition of Belgium and the special problem of Brussels.
Describe the major social groups of Sri Lanka and where they are concentrated.
Identify the majoritarian measures adopted in Sri Lanka after 1948 and explain the idea of majoritarianism.
Explain how majoritarian policies led to Tamil alienation, demands for autonomy and civil war.
State the main elements of the Belgian power-sharing model and explain how they prevent domination by one community.
Explain the composition and powers of the community government in Belgium.
Explain the prudential reasons for power sharing, such as reducing conflict and ensuring stability.
Explain the moral reason that power sharing is the very spirit of democracy.
Explain horizontal distribution of power among organs of government and the system of checks and balances.
Explain vertical (federal) division of power among different levels of government.
Identify power sharing among social groups and among political parties, pressure groups and movements.
Define federalism and distinguish a federal system from a unitary one.
Identify the key features of a federal system of government.
Distinguish 'coming together' from 'holding together' federations with examples.

topics.title: What makes India a federal country?
topics.ncert_sections: What makes India a federal country?

concepts.learning_objective: Classify subjects under the Union, State and Concurrent Lists and explain residuary powers.
Explain why some States have special powers and how Union Territories are governed.
Describe how the Union-State power-sharing arrangement can be changed and the role of courts.

topics.title: Linguistic States and language policy
topics.ncert_sections: How is federalism practised? (Linguistic States; Language policy; Linguistic diversity of India)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the creation of linguistic States tested and strengthened Indian federalism.
Describe India's language policy and the accommodation shown towards non-Hindi speakers.
Interpret Census data on the linguistic diversity of India.
Explain how one-party dominance weakened State autonomy in the early decades.
Analyse how regional parties and coalition governments after 1990 strengthened federal power sharing.
Explain the meaning of decentralisation and the reasons for it.
State the main provisions of the 1992 amendment on local government.

topics.title: Rural and urban local government at work
topics.ncert_sections: Decentralisation in India (Panchayati raj; urban local bodies; An experiment in Brazil)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of rural local government from the gram panchayat to the zilla parishad.
Identify urban local bodies and their political heads.
Evaluate the achievements and difficulties of local self-government.

topics.title: Gender division and the public/private division

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that gender division is based on social expectations and stereotypes, not on biology.
Describe the sexual division of labour and its effect on women's role in public life.
Identify the aims of feminist movements and the meaning of the term feminist.

topics.title: Discrimination and disadvantage faced by women in India
topics.ncert_sections: Gender and politics (patriarchy, literacy, wages, child sex ratio)

concepts.learning_objective: Define patriarchy and relate it to the disadvantages women face in India.
Interpret evidence on unpaid household work and unequal pay for women.
Explain the meaning of child sex ratio and why it has declined in India.
Describe the low level of women's representation in India's legislatures.
Explain how reservation of seats aims to increase women's representation in elected bodies.
Distinguish acceptable roles of religion in politics from communal politics.
Explain the beliefs on which communal politics is based and why they are flawed.
Identify the various forms that communalism takes in politics.
State the constitutional provisions that make India a secular state.
Evaluate why a secular Constitution is necessary but not sufficient to combat communalism.

topics.title: Caste inequalities
topics.ncert_sections: Caste and politics; Caste inequalities; Caste inequality today

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the features of the traditional caste system.
Explain the factors that have weakened caste hierarchy and the aspects of caste that persist.
Interpret evidence on the link between caste and economic status.

topics.title: Caste in politics and politics in caste
topics.ncert_sections: Caste in politics; Politics in caste

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways in which caste enters electoral politics.
Explain why caste alone cannot determine election results in India.
Analyse how politics influences caste identities and evaluate caste politics in a democracy.

topics.title: Meaning and components of a political party
topics.ncert_sections: Why do we need political parties? - Meaning

concepts.learning_objective: Define a political party and explain why parties try to persuade people about their policies.
Explain how parties reflect political divisions and involve partisanship.
Identify the three components of a political party.
Describe the functions parties perform, from offering policies to providing access to government.
Distinguish the ways parties in different countries select their candidates.
Explain the role of parties that lose elections and how parties shape public opinion.

topics.title: Necessity of political parties and popular participation
topics.ncert_sections: Necessity; Popular participation in political parties

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why modern representative democracies cannot exist without political parties.
Interpret survey evidence on trust in and participation in political parties in India.

topics.title: Party systems: how many parties should we have?
topics.ncert_sections: How many parties should we have?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish one-party, two-party and multiparty systems with examples.
Explain what an alliance or front is in a multiparty system.
Explain why a party system evolves from a country's circumstances and cannot simply be chosen.
Apply the Election Commission's criteria for recognising State and national parties.
Identify the founding, ideas and support base of India's recognised national parties.
Explain how the rise of State parties has strengthened federalism and democracy.
Explain the lack of internal democracy and dynastic succession as challenges to parties.
Explain the growing role of money and muscle power in parties during elections.
Analyse why voters often do not get a meaningful choice among parties.
Evaluate the effects of the constitutional amendment against defection.
Describe the Supreme Court and Election Commission orders aimed at reforming parties.
Evaluate suggested reforms and the role of citizens in reforming parties.

topics.title: How do we assess democracy's outcomes?

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the reasons democracy is considered better than other forms of government and the gap between its principle and practice.
Explain that democracy is only a form of government that creates conditions which citizens must use to achieve goals.
Explain how democracy produces a government that follows procedures, is transparent and is accountable to citizens.
Evaluate the argument that the delay caused by deliberation makes democratic government inefficient.
Explain why democratic government is legitimate and enjoys overwhelming popular support.
Interpret evidence comparing economic growth rates of democracies and dictatorships between 1950 and 2000.
Identify the factors other than the form of government on which economic development depends.
Distinguish political equality in voting from the growing economic inequalities found in democracies.
Interpret data on the share of national income held by the top and bottom 20 per cent in selected democracies.
Analyse why democratically elected governments have not been very successful in reducing poverty.
Explain how democracies develop procedures to negotiate social differences and prevent them from turning violent.
State the two conditions a democracy must fulfil to accommodate social diversity.

topics.title: Dignity and freedom of the citizens

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how recognition of equality in democracy strengthens the struggles of women and disadvantaged castes.
Interpret why public complaints about democracy are a sign of its success in turning subjects into citizens.
